groups.name: The Gentlemen
groups.profile: Also tracked as Storm-2697. RaaS that appeared in July–August 2025 and offers affiliates a 90% revenue share; Go-based locker for Windows, Linux, NAS and BSD. Ransomware.live says a compromised C2 server exposed more than 1,570 linked victims. Tooling per Ransomware.live: AnyDesk, credential dumpers, NTLM relay, rclone. Today it posted 24 victims in about four hours (10:12–14:24 UTC on RansomLook), each with a long company profile and no screenshot or data inventory. Ransomware.live has not ingested a Gentlemen posting since 2026-10-31, so every row is RansomLook-only.
groups.countries: Brazil (3), Switzerland (2), Spain (2), United Kingdom (2), United States (2), Netherlands, Ukraine, South Africa, Venezuela, France, New Zealand, Canada, Germany, not disclosed (5)
groups.sectors: Not disclosed (profiles describe logistics, manufacturing, education, healthcare, legal, IT, real estate, public health)

groups.name: Orova
groups.profile: Leak site tracked by Ransomware.live since 2026-07-07; no published tactics profile. Four Singapore/Malaysia-heavy postings at 12:23 UTC, three with only a one-paragraph company blurb.

groups.name: Akira
groups.profile: Active since March 2023, widely linked to former Conti members; double extortion, Windows and ESXi lockers. Known for exploiting VPN appliances without MFA. Today's three posts all promise uploads, two with volumes (130 GB, 945 GB).

groups.name: Interlock
groups.profile: First observed September 2024; double extortion against healthcare, government, education and technology in North America and Europe (CISA advisory July 2025). Known for fake browser-update / ClickFix lures. Third straight day of paired postings; today it is two US school districts, citing FERPA and PowerSchool data.

groups.name: Qilin
groups.profile: Also known as Agenda. Golang/Rust RaaS first observed July 2022 and the most prolific leak site on Ransomware.live; double extortion, with the operator controlling encryption modes. A quiet day after ten postings in №71.

groups.name: BYOD
groups.profile: New leak site tracked by Ransomware.live since 2026-10-05; no published profile.

groups.name: Hyflock
groups.profile: New group tracked since 2026-10-13; Ransomware.live advises caution until claims are independently verified.

groups.name: NightSpire
groups.profile: Emerged March 2025; 250+ claimed victims across retail, manufacturing, healthcare, finance and education, with ransom deadlines as short as two days.

groups.name: PEAR
groups.profile: Pure Extraction And Ransom (PEAR), tracked since 2025-08-05; a data-theft-and-extortion team that says it works privately with no affiliates.

groups.name: Redact
groups.profile: Leak site tracked by Ransomware.live since 2026-06-28; no published profile. Claiming a $2B-revenue US law firm is a high-profile claim for a little-known group.

groups.name: SafePay
groups.profile: Emerged September 2024; disavows the RaaS model and runs operations in-house; 300+ claimed victims by mid-2025.
